newsitem.title: UK: North Sea trade picks up but Brent overhang remain.
newsitem.headline: North Sea trade picks up but Brent overhang remain.

text.p: North Sea crude trade picked up on Thursday as better margins encouraged refinery buyers but spot differentials showed little sign of recovering amid a persistent overhang of Dated Brent, traders said.
The sale of eight April 11-21 Brent cargoes by BP to Shell did nothing to remove the pressure from the front end of the market, they said.
"Margins are healthy as they have been for a while now but basically there's still plenty of oil around," said a trader.
Traders said Shell could use some of the Brents in its own refining system and would explore arbitrage options.

But with U.S. Gulf buyers unwilling to pay much more than May WTI -$1.00/-$0.90 cents a barrel for the benchmark grade as supply of competing crudes remains more than adequate, other traders were sceptical the arbitrage would work.

Dated Brent continued to trade this week's range as an April 10-12 cargo moved between traders at May Brent -93 cents and other grades, including Oseberg and Forties, remained pegged back at depressed levels.
Brent CFDs held out little prospect of an improvement, next week trading three to five cents weaker. May Brent shed 26 cents to $18.25 a barrel but intermonth spreads were broadly steady.
Better margins in the Mediterranean were also stimulating modest buying interest, lending support to sour Urals but refiners were only prepared to bid around Dated Brent -$1.50.
The margin for a complex refinery processing Urals rose on Wednesday to $2.60 a barrel, the highest level since November 1996 and a full dollar higher than in early March.
A mid-April Urals changed hands late on Wednesday at a $1.37 discount to Dated Brent cost and freight Augusta, traders said.
Other recent trades included a Urals loading April 18-20 at Dated -$1.37 and another loading April 9-11 at Dated -$1.38 cif Augusta.
